assertion.en: A person who has just turned 18 can vote at any polling station, even if their name is not on the electoral roll.

reason.en: Electoral rolls are organised polling station-wise, and only those whose names appear on the roll are allowed to vote.

a.en: The Assertion is false. A person whose name is not on the roll cannot vote, so the Reason cannot explain it.

b.en: The Assertion is false, so the two statements are not both true. The Reason says the opposite of the Assertion.

c.en: The Reason is true: only names on the roll may vote. It is the Assertion that is false.

explanation.en: The Assertion is false and the Reason is true. Turning 18 lets a citizen join the roll, but it does not put the name there. Only those whose names appear on the roll are allowed to vote.

hints.en: Decide whether each statement is true by itself.
Can a person vote if their name is missing from the roll?
